transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Um… I guess I’m here because I’ve been worrying a lot—probably more than I should. It feels like everything piles up at once: my marriage, work and whether I’m starting to slip there, bills, stuff around the house I keep not finishing… and then I start thinking I’m just failing as a husband and a dad. I know that may sound a little dramatic, but I can’t seem to shut it off.
Can you tell me more about when these worries started and if they seem to happen most days or more in certain situations?

Yeah… I think it’s been about nine months, maybe around then. It started when the cloud migration at work really ramped up, and at the same time the arguments at home started becoming more of a regular thing. I don’t want to make it sound like it was all at once or anything, but that’s when I started noticing the worrying was there most days.
Have you noticed feeling down or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, like hobbies or time with your family?

Um… I don’t think so, not in a big way. I mean, I get worn out and maybe I’m not as present as I’d like to be sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’ve lost interest in my family or anything. I still want to do those things. I’m not sure if that answers what you’re asking.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms like restlessness, trouble sleeping, or muscle tension along with these worries?

Yeah… I mean, it’s probably not the worst thing, but I do feel kind of wound tight most of the day. Like my shoulders are locked up, and I’m bracing for something even when nothing is happening.

I catch myself pacing between meetings sometimes, or if I’m at chess club I’ll be tapping the pieces because sitting still feels… I don’t know, almost impossible. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you noticed feeling fatigued or low on energy most days, even when you haven’t been doing much physically or mentally taxing?

I’m not totally sure. I mean, I do feel tired sometimes, but I guess I’ve been assuming that’s just normal with work and life stuff. I wouldn’t want to overstate it.

I haven’t really noticed being low-energy most days in a clear way, if that makes sense. It’s more like… I can usually still get through what I need to do. Is that the kind of distinction you’re asking about?
Do you find that your worrying feels excessive or hard to control, even when you try to stop thinking about things?

Yeah… I guess it can be hard to control. I try not to make it into a big deal, because I know everyone worries, but sometimes even when I tell myself, “Just focus on the code in front of you,” it doesn’t really stop.

One concern kind of hooks into the next, and then I’m way ahead of myself—like a bad review turns into me losing my job, and then my family being worse off because of me. I know that probably sounds extreme, and I can usually tell myself it’s not logical, but it still keeps going. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Would you say your worrying and physical symptoms have been happening almost every day for at least six months, or more in response to specific stressful events in the past year?

I think… yeah, it’s been more than just a short stressful patch. I’d say about nine months now.

It kind of started when the cloud migration at work ramped up, and around the same time the arguments at home started becoming more regular. I don’t want to make it sound like every single minute has been bad, but the worrying and the keyed-up feeling have been there most days since then, I think. Does that answer it?
Have these worries and the way you’ve been feeling physically made it harder for you to function in your job, your relationships, or other important areas of your life?

Yeah… I think it has, more than I’d like to admit.

At work, my manager has started writing down or documenting things I’ve missed—mostly architectural details that I should’ve caught. I’m trying not to make excuses for it, but I know that’s not great.

And at home, I’ll start things and not finish them, or I’m kind of physically there but distracted, and then the arguments just… keep escalating. I don’t want to overstate it, but it’s definitely affecting things. Does that make sense as an answer?
Would you say that you feel excessive anxiety or worry on more days than not, even when there isn't a specific stressor happening at that moment?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like I’m panicking every second or anything, but it’s kind of there even when nothing specific is happening.

I came in because I feel like I can’t stop worrying about everything at once—my marriage, whether I’m slipping at work, bills, the house projects I keep dropping, and whether I’m basically failing as a husband and father. Even if one thing settles down, my mind just moves to the next thing.

Is that what you mean by more days than not?
Have you noticed yourself becoming more irritable or easily annoyed, especially in situations where you might not have reacted that way before?

I’m not totally sure. I mean, I don’t think of myself as an angry person, and I try not to snap at people.

Maybe I’ve been a little shorter than usual sometimes, but… I don’t know if that counts as irritability or just being stressed. I’d like to think I’m mostly keeping it under control.

Is that the kind of thing you’re asking about?
Have you noticed any trouble concentrating or your mind going blank more often, especially when you're not particularly tired or distracted?

Yeah… that one, yes. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like I’m completely unable to work, because I am still getting things done, but it’s been happening more than I’m comfortable with.

During sprint planning or code reviews, I’ll read the same design note three or four times and somehow still miss details. It’s like part of my brain is technically looking at the screen, but another part is off thinking about what I forgot to do at home or how badly the next argument is going to go.

So… yes, concentration has been harder. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
